content:
The spectrum is dominated by four peaks: three closely spaced C-H stretching bands at 2879, 2916, and 2937 cm⁻¹, and a weaker band at 1450 cm⁻¹.

The C-H stretch region (2850–2960 cm⁻¹) with multiple resolved peaks is characteristic of aliphatic CH₂ and CH₃ groups. The 1450 cm⁻¹ band corresponds to CH₂/CH₃ bending (scissoring/asymmetric deformation), which is a standard assignment for saturated aliphatic chains (GFQ-003 supports C-H stretching at 2900–3100 cm⁻¹ and C-H bending at 1300–1500 cm⁻¹).

The spectrum is notably simple — only aliphatic C-H features, no aromatic C-H, no N-H stretch (~3300 cm⁻¹), no strong O-H (~3400 cm⁻¹), no azide (~2090 cm⁻¹), no C=C or C=N in the 1600–1700 region. This rules out candidates with prominent NH₂/NH groups (which would show N-H stretches in Raman, though sometimes weak), azide groups (candidates 6, 7 have N₃), and cyclopropyl rings (which add ring-breathing modes around 1000–1050 cm⁻¹).

Comparing the candidates structurally:

- Candidates 6 and 7 contain azide groups (N₃), which would show a strong ~2090 cm⁻¹ Raman band — absent here, so these are excluded.
- Candidates with cyclopropyl rings (2, 4, 5, 8) would show ring-breathing modes near 1000–1050 cm⁻¹ — not observed.
- Candidate 1 (CCCOCCN) is a simple aliphatic ether-amine: propyl group attached to an oxygen, then ethylamine. It has an extended aliphatic chain (CH₃CH₂CH₂-) giving multiple CH₂/CH₃ stretches, an O-CH₂ group, and a terminal CH₂NH₂. The ether C-O-C stretch would appear around 1000–1150 cm⁻¹ but may be weak or not detected as a prominent peak. The dominant Raman features would be the aliphatic C-H stretches (~2870–2940 cm⁻¹) and CH₂/CH₃ bending (~1450 cm⁻¹) — matching well.
- Candidate 9 (CCNCCO) is N-ethylaminoethanol — a shorter chain with N-ethyl and ethanolamine. Fewer CH₂ groups, simpler C-H region.
- Candidate 10 (C[C@@H](CO)CCCN) has a branched chain with a primary amine and hydroxymethyl group.
- Candidate 3 (CCN(C)CCN) is a tertiary diamine — would show more complex C-N stretching features.

Candidate 1 (CCCOCCN, 3-ethoxypropylamine / propyl-oxyethylamine) has the most aliphatic carbon content among the simpler candidates, giving the richest set of CH₂ and CH₃ groups to produce the observed three-band C-H stretch pattern and the 1450 cm⁻¹ bending mode, with no interfering functional groups that would add peaks absent from the spectrum. It is also ranked first by retrieval similarity, which serves as a useful prior.

SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.52
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows only aliphatic C-H stretches at 2879, 2916, and 2937 cm⁻¹ and a CH₂/CH₃ bending mode at 1450 cm⁻¹ (consistent with GFQ-003). The absence of azide (~2090 cm⁻¹), aromatic C-H, and cyclopropyl ring modes excludes candidates 6, 7, and the cyclopropane-containing molecules. Candidate 1 (CCCOCCN) has the richest aliphatic chain profile among the remaining options, consistent with multiple resolved C-H stretching bands, and ranks first by retrieval similarity.
